meta.preheader: NIFTY 50 rose 1.85% to 25,819.25 on Wednesday as FMCG gained 3.79%; foreign investors bought ₹4,479 crore (provisional); the rupee closed at 92.16.
meta.subject: Kubeerra Market Brief · Thu 26 Nov: NIFTY 50 rises 1.85% to 25,819.25; FMCG up 3.79%

brief: The NIFTY 50 rose 1.85% to 25,819.25 and the Sensex 1.82% to 83,938.28 on Wednesday 25 Nov, recovering Monday's fall; Nifty Bank rose 1.79% to 63,703.25 (HDFC Sky, Upstox, Liquide).

Nifty FMCG rose 3.79% as Hindustan Unilever gained 6.08%; Nifty Metal fell 2.04% and APL Apollo Tubes 11.62% after it and Tata Steel said they were open to reviewing their deal (HDFC Sky, Upstox, CNBC-TV18).

Foreign investors bought a net ₹4,479 crore and domestic institutions ₹4,019 crore (Kotak Neo; provisional). The rupee closed at a provisional 92.16 per dollar, 69 paise stronger and its strongest close in eight months (PTI).

After India's close, the US proposed Section 301 tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods; India's Department of Commerce rejected the excess-capacity finding (Business Standard). The Nasdaq fell 0.62% and the Dow rose 0.33%; US markets are closed today for Thanksgiving.
IBJA's Wednesday afternoon rate put gold at ₹1,21,038 per 10 g, down 3.13% from Monday, and silver at ₹1,42,945 per kg, down 6.34%; Brent settled at $94.61 a barrel, up 3.5% (IBJA, The Nation).

outlook.headline: Foreign buying, crude, US tariffs and rate decisions frame the week

drivers.title: Foreign buying
drivers.text: Foreign investors bought a net ₹1,22,101 crore of Indian shares from 1 to 25 November (Kotak Neo; provisional); PTI, citing NSDL data to 20 Nov, called November's inflow the largest on record. Foreign flows reach index heavyweights and the rupee.

drivers.title: Crude and the rupee
drivers.text: Brent settled at $94.61 on Wednesday, up 3.5%, after the Houthis said they had attacked Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery (The Nation); during Indian hours it had been lower, and the rupee closed at a provisional 92.16 per dollar (PTI). Oil reaches India through the import bill, the rupee and fuel inflation.

drivers.title: US tariff proposal
drivers.text: The US Trade Representative proposed Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies, up to 25% on Indian goods and 17% if a trade deal is concluded; India's Department of Commerce rejected the excess-capacity finding and said the notice is under examination (Business Standard, PTI). Tariffs reach India through export-oriented sectors and the trade balance.

drivers.title: Rate expectations
drivers.text: In a Reuters poll taken 13 to 20 Nov, 56 of 61 economists expected the RBI to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.75% on 4 Dec. Policy rates reach bank lending rates, deposit rates and bond yields.

drivers.title: Growth data
drivers.text: July to September GDP is due on 30 Nov; Deccan Herald reports a Finance Ministry nowcast of 7.35%, against 7.8% in April to June. Growth figures shape earnings estimates and feed into the RBI's decision.

global_cues.title: US shares
global_cues.text: On Wednesday the Dow rose 0.33% after falling more than 1,100 points during the day, while the Nasdaq fell 0.62% as chip stocks fell on doubts about AI spending (The Motley Fool, Yahoo Finance). US moves reach India through foreign flows and US-exposed sectors such as IT.

global_cues.title: US inflation and the Fed
global_cues.text: October core PCE inflation was 3.3% a year, against a consensus estimate of 3.2% (Scotsman Guide), and CME FedWatch put the chance of a quarter-point Fed rise in December near 98%. US rates reach India through the dollar, the rupee and emerging-market flows.

global_cues.title: Asian markets
global_cues.text: On Wednesday the Kospi fell 6.16% and the Nikkei 2.78% as chip stocks were sold (TradingKey); early on Thursday Reuters reported both higher. Asia sets the regional tone for Indian trading.

events.title: US Federal Reserve meeting
events.text: The decision is due on 9 Dec, US time (Federal Reserve); CME FedWatch puts the chance of a quarter-point rise near 98% (Scotsman Guide).

global.headline: Wall Street recovered most of an early fall on Wednesday as chip stocks pulled Asia lower; the Kospi fell 6.16%
global.note: Closes are for Wednesday 25 Nov. AP rounds the S&P 500's fall to 0.3%; the 0.25% shown is from its points change. US stock markets are closed on Thursday 26 Nov for Thanksgiving and close early on Friday.

us.title: The session
us.text: The S&P 500 was down as much as 3.2% during the day before closing about 0.3% lower; the Dow rose 0.3% and the Nasdaq fell 0.6% (AP). Chip stocks led the losses as doubts over AI spending returned, and Nvidia closed about 3.9% lower (Yahoo Finance).

us.title: Data and tariffs
us.text: October PCE inflation was 3.8% a year (core 3.3%), third-quarter GDP growth was revised up to 4.3%, and the administration proposed new tariffs on China, the EU and 12 other partners (Yahoo Finance).

us.title: Bonds and the dollar
us.text: The 10-year Treasury yield fell about 8 basis points to about 4.85% and the dollar index eased about 0.1% to about 103.7 (Longbridge, ChainCatcher).

events.title: A December Fed rise priced in
events.text: After the October PCE data, markets fully priced a December rate rise (Kitco News); the Fed meets on 8 and 9 Dec. The channel to India: the dollar, the rupee and foreign flows.

events.title: New US tariff proposals
events.text: The US proposed Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies, including China, the EU, India, Japan and South Korea; a comment period and hearing come first (Euronews, Business Standard). The channel to India: export demand and global risk appetite.

events.title: Gulf supply risk and OPEC+
events.text: Yemen's Houthis said they attacked Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery, and OPEC+ meets on 29 Nov on 2027 output (The Nation). The channel to India: the import bill, fuel inflation and the rupee.

metals.headline: IBJA's Wednesday afternoon rate put gold at ₹1,21,038 per 10 g, down 3.13% from Monday; silver fell 6.34%

international.label: Spot gold, 25 Nov
international.detail: New York close (Longbridge), after touching its lowest level since 2025 during the session; FXBrokerTrust gives $3,588.40

commentary.text: IBJA published no rates on the 24 Nov holiday, so the change shown is from Monday afternoon's rates.
Kitco News said gold fell to its lowest in more than a year on Wednesday after US PCE data showed inflation rising, and markets fully priced a December Fed rise.
David Meger of High Ridge Futures said inflation well above the Fed's target makes further rises more likely, which weighs on gold, Kitco News reported.
FXBrokerTrust credited bargain hunting and pre-Thanksgiving position adjustments for the later recovery, with modest help from a softer dollar, lower Treasury yields and the Houthi claims.

stories.headline: IRDAI sets up a panel to review insurance commission proposals

category_explainer.category: Dynamic Asset Allocation or Balanced Advantage
category_explainer.text: Under SEBI's scheme categories, as revised in February 2026 and reported by Upstox, a dynamic asset allocation or balanced advantage fund is an open-ended hybrid scheme that invests in equity and debt and manages the split between them dynamically. Because that split changes over time, such a fund carries share-price risk on its equity part and interest-rate and credit risk on its debt part, in proportions that vary. Each scheme's riskometer level and risk factors are in the fund house's own documents.

learn.title: What a riskometer level tells you
paragraphs: SEBI's riskometer places every mutual fund scheme at one of six levels: Low, Low to Moderate, Moderate, Moderately High, High and Very High (SEBI circular, October 2020).

The fund house sets the level from the risk of the securities the scheme holds and reviews it every month, publishing it with the portfolio on its own website and AMFI's; if the level changes, unitholders are told (SEBI). For shares the assessment looks at factors such as market size, volatility and liquidity, and for bonds at credit, interest-rate and liquidity risk (Mutual Funds Sahi Hai).

The level appears in the scheme information document, the key information memorandum and the application form, next to the scheme's name (SEBI). It describes the risk of what a scheme holds today; it is not a measure of returns, and it can change as the portfolio changes.
